macro.label: S&P 500 at 7,411.98
macro.text: Down 0.61% last week and now below its 50-day average, a sign buyers are getting careful. Consider wider call strikes and accepting less cash for them this week.

macro.label: VIX at 18.58
macro.text: The index is calm while individual companies are not. Favor selling on individual quality names over index funds, since that's where the premium is.

macro.label: 10-year yield at 4.68%
macro.text: Rich bond yields are pulling money out of utilities, REITs and telecoms. Give more room on strikes for any of those you hold.

macro.label: 3-month T-bill at 3.730%
macro.text: The risk-free bar every trade below needs to clearly beat once you allow for what could go wrong. Cash is a valid position while you wait.

days.name: Monday
days.rule: Monday-Tuesday window: sell healthcare and industrials names while the calendar is calm, ahead of Wednesday’s Fed decision. These 5 aren’t tied to a single day, so place them either Monday or Tuesday.

trades.note: Healthcare; the stock would need to fall 8.6% before this strike matters.
Healthcare; the biggest cushion on the list, though it ties up a lot of cash.
Industrials (work-uniform rental); nothing about AI spending touches this business.
Healthcare; barely moves when the broader market does, which is the point this week.
Healthcare; only 3.8% above today’s price, so be ready to part with the shares.

days.name: Tuesday
days.rule: Same Monday-Tuesday window as Monday, same 5 names: the last calm day before the Fed speaks Wednesday afternoon.

trades.note: Healthcare; the stock would need to fall 8.6% before this strike matters.
Healthcare; the biggest cushion on the list, though it ties up a lot of cash.
Industrials (work-uniform rental); nothing about AI spending touches this business.
Healthcare; barely moves when the broader market does, which is the point this week.

days.name: Wednesday
days.rule: Treat today as a no-new-trades day. Nothing opened today beats waiting until tomorrow. If anything expiring Aug 3 or 7 is showing a profit, consider closing it this morning rather than carrying it through two more nights of earnings headlines.
days.event: Key event: Fed rate decision, 11:00 AM Pacific. Microsoft and Meta report after the close.

days.name: Thursday
days.rule: Wait until 7:00 AM Pacific before opening anything. Bid/ask spreads widen right after the inflation number, so half an hour of patience is worth real money on a large position. Once that settles, sell the financials and remaining industrials below.
days.event: Key event: core inflation (PCE) data, 5:30 AM Pacific, the second of this week’s two "walls." Apple and Amazon report after the close tonight.

trades.note: Industrials; the lowest chance of assignment on the list, roughly 1-in-5.
Financials; already reported, and banks tend to do better if rates rise.
Communication services; jumped 6% Friday on its results, so this sells into a name that just ran.
Financials; the best return for the cash tied up of anything on this list.

days.name: Friday
days.rule: Apple and Amazon earnings risk has cleared. Sell the tech names below, the richest premium of the week now that both walls are behind us.
days.event: Apple and Amazon reported Thursday night; both risks are now behind these names.

trades.note: Technology; pays the most per day of any clean name here, with the strike only 4.4% away.
Technology; the largest single premium on the list, and the highest chance of the shares getting called away.
Communication services; already reported and already punished, which is exactly why the premium is still this good.
